# Ferrow House Residency, August 2026

Twelve days at Ferrow House, 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-21, to finish part one of the third draft of The Salt Choir. It worked: part one (chapters 1 to 12, 1924 to 1926) was finished on the evening of 2026-08-20 at 38,600 words.

## The plan

One goal, written into the application ([[ferrow-house-residency-plan]]): part one finished, nothing else. No new research, no part two, no publicity. Email once a day after supper.

## How the days went

- Writing 07:00 to 12:30, walk, revision 15:00 to 17:30, supper at 19:00 with the other residents and [[yusuf-demirel]].
- Words rewritten or new: 17,500 on arrival, 38,600 on 2026-08-20. The best day was 2,900 words (chapter 10, the collier rescue); the worst was 600 (chapter 7, Tobias's first war scene, which I rewrote three times).
- The anachronism check on part one ran on 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-15 alongside the writing, with three fixes: the coxswain's election moved to the lifeboat house, lifejackets tied with tapes rather than buckled, and the wireless set confined to the Institute ([[saltmarrow-anachronism-log]]).

## What I learned

- Narrow goals survive residencies; broad ones dissolve into reading. Recorded as [[residencies-are-for-finishing-not-starting]].
- I write more in the afternoon than I believed, when there is no class and no inbox.
- The prologue question did not move: I wrote the four pages again on the last morning and they are better, but I still cannot answer Callum's point that they give the ending away. That belongs with the draft, not here.

## Afterwards

- Report to Yusuf sent 2026-08-28.
- Last-day notes in [[recaps/daily/2026/2026-08-21]].
